akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي﴾: it is read with hamza and without hamza; [and] they are two dialectal variants. The hamza is dropped because this word is used so often.

akhfash:2-2.t: And He said ﴿فَذَلِكَ ٱلَّذِي يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ﴾: He means "he pushes him away from his right" (يدفعه عن حقه). You say "دَعَعْتُه" "أَدُعُّه" "دَعّاً".

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ﴾: the recompense and the reckoning; that is, do you know him? And if you do not know him:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿فَذَلِكَ﴾ — with «هو» implied after the fāʾ — ﴿الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ﴾, that is, pushes him away roughly from his due,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَلَا يَحُضُّ﴾ himself or others ﴿عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ﴾, that is, feeding him. It was revealed concerning al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ﴾: heedless, delaying it beyond its time,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ﴾ in the prayer and elsewhere,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ﴾: such as the needle, the axe, the cooking pot and the bowl.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فَذلِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.
﴿يَدُعُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْيَتِيمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾ is negative. ﴿يَحُضُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى طَعامِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمِسْكِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ the fāʾ is causative (li-l-sababiyya); ﴿ويل﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of المصلين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿ساهُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the preceding الذين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُراؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the first object is omitted, its implied form being «الناس» (the people). ﴿الْماعُونَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَدُعُّ) means: he pushes away with violence and harshness. In al-Mukhtār: "daʿʿa, of the pattern of radda." Ibn Durayd said: daʿʿahu and daḥḥahu have one meaning; and a woman is daʿūʿ and daḥūḥ. He recited:
قبيح بالعجوز إذا تغدّت ... من البرنيّ واللبن الصريح
بتغّيها الرجال وفي صلاها ... مواقع كل فيشلة دحوح
(Ugly in an old woman, when she has had her midday meal of barnī dates and pure milk, / that she should seek men, while in her haunches are the places of every thrusting [member]; the text of the second verse is obscure.)
And Thaʿlab recited, on the authority of Ibn al-Aʿrābī:
قد أغتدي والليل في حريمه ... معسكرا في الغرّ من نجومه والصبح قد نسّم في أديمه ... يدعّه بضفّتي حيزومه
دعّ الربيب لحيتي يتيمه
(I set out at dawn while the night is still in its precinct, encamped among its bright stars, and the morning has breathed upon its surface, pushing it with the two sides of its chest, as the stepson shoves the beard of his orphan [stepchild].)
(الْماعُونَ) In al-Mukhtār: "al-māʿūn is a comprehensive name for the household's utilities, such as the pot and the axe and the like." The wording of Ibn Khālawayh is: "Al-māʿūn: obedience; al-māʿūn: zakāt; al-māʿūn: water; al-māʿūn: the ḥāl [? 'state']; al-māʿūn: the bucket, the fire-striker, the axe, fire, salt, and the like of what belongs to the dwellings. The dwellings were called māʿūn only because a traveller who has these things with him can settle wherever he wishes." Al-Rāʿī said:
قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا ... ماعونهم ويضيعوا التهليلا
(A people who, on Islam, had not yet withheld their māʿūn and had not yet neglected the declaration of tahlīl [lā ilāha illā llāh].)

* I'rab:
(أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ) The hamza is for interrogation, and together with (رأيت) it means "tell me", as has often been stated before. It is also permissible that the seeing be of the heart, in which case it takes two objects, the first being the relative noun and the second omitted; the meaning is "Do you know who the one is who denies the Judgement?" It is also said that the seeing is of the eye, in which case there is no need to posit an object. (فَذلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa) because it introduces an apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being "if you do not know him, then that is he." Al-Samīn put it as "if you seek knowledge of him, then that is he." (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) is its khabar, and the clause (يدع اليتيم) is the ṣila (relative clause). It is strange that Ibn Khālawayh parsed (الذي) as an adjective of (ذلك) and did not mention the khabar at all, though he said that (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ. There are other views and parsings mentioned by the exegetes; we have passed over them, as they are merely forced. (وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative. (يحض) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", i.e., the one who pushes the orphan away; (على طعام المسكين) are two elements attached to (يحض). (فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ) The fāʾ is again the eloquent fāʾ, i.e., "if you have learned that he is characterised by these attributes, then woe", or "if the matter is so, then woe". This is preferable to al-Samīn's statement that it is the fāʾ of causation, which he explained by saying: "The fāʾ is of causation, i.e., the invocation of woe upon them is caused by these blameworthy attributes." (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ and (للمصلين) is its khabar. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ) (الذين) is an adjective of (للمصلين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن صلاتهم) is attached to (ساهون); and the nominal clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of (الذين). We consider far-fetched the view of those who interpreted heedlessness "of" the prayer in the verse as heedlessness "in" the prayer, for heedlessness within it is neither a sin nor a reprehensible act for which the one who forgets is threatened with woe; every believer is liable to forget in his prayer, and this forgetfulness is made good by the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) or by the sunnas and supererogatory prayers, as established in fiqh. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُراؤُنَ وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْماعُونَ) (الذين) is a badal (substitute) for the first (الذين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يراءون) is the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of (الذين). The clause (يمنعون الماعون) is conjoined to (يراءون), falling within the scope of the ṣila. The first object of (يمنعون) is omitted, i.e., "people" or "those who ask", and (الماعون) is its second object.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "أرأيتك الذى"; the kāf is a ṣila (connective, i.e. a redundant addition) that may be present or absent, and the meaning is the same.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ﴾.
From دععت, and it is يُدعّ: he pushes him away from his right and wrongs him. Likewise: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحُضُّ﴾.
I.e.: he does not attend to feeding the poor, nor does he enjoin it.

farraa:4-4.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾, meaning the hypocrites; ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلاَتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ﴾: he says: heedless (لاهون). Ibn ʿAbbās explained it so, and so I saw it in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd].

farraa:6-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ﴾.
If people see them, they pray; and if no one sees them, they abandon prayer. ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ ٱلْمَاعُونَ﴾: He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ḥibbān narrated to me, with his chain of transmission; he said: "الماعون" is every kind of common kindness, even mentioning the bowl, the cooking pot and the axe.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, who said: "الماعون" is the zakāt.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, the like of it. He said: And I heard one of the Arabs say: «الماعون» is water; and he recited to me concerning it:
* يَمجُّ صَبيرهُ الماعُونَ صَبًا *
(Its white cloud-mass spews forth the water in a downpour.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: I do not remember its first half. «الصبير» is cloud.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «أرأيت»: meaning "tell me", and it is transitive to two objects: the first is «الذي», and the second is an implied (muqaddar) interrogative clause: is he not deserving of punishment?; the place where it is implied is after His saying {الْمِسْكِينِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «فذلك الذي»: the apodosis of an implied condition (jawāb sharṭ muqaddar), i.e.: if you want to know him, then that is he.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and «ويل»: mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of للمصلين; the preposition «عن صلاتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ساهون».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «الذين»: badal (substitute) of the preceding relative noun.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (أرأيت الذي): whoever lightened the hamza made it between the hamza and the alif; and it was said: he substituted an alif for it. That is permissible even though a quiescent letter follows it, because a quiescent letter and a doubled letter may come after the alif according to the position of all the grammarians; and a quiescent letter that is not doubled may come after it according to the position of Yūnus, Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans, while Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad prohibited it. Eliding the hamza is permissible, and al-Kisāʾī read it so. (أرأيت) may be from seeing with the heart [i.e. knowing], with the second object omitted — there is remoteness in this in terms of the i'rab and the omission, though it is more fitting in meaning than seeing with the eye; or it may be from seeing with the eye, so there is no need for an omission.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿أرأيت﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative, and «رأيت» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). What is meant by ﴿أرأيت﴾ is "tell me" (أخبرني), and in that case it is transitive to two objects, the first being ﴿الذي﴾ and the second omitted, its implied form being: "who is he?" (من هو), or "is he not deserving of punishment?" (أليس مستحقا للعذاب). Or the seeing is visual, so the verb is transitive to one object. The clause ﴿أرأيت﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يكذب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿يكذب﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿بالدين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكذب﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فذلك﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), because it is the answer of an implied condition, the implied wording being: "if you do not know him, then that is..." (إن لم تعرفه فذلك), or "if you seek knowledge of him, then that is..." (إن طلبت علمه فذلك), or "if you consider him, then that is..." (إن تأملته فذلك). In «ذلك», «ذا» is a demonstrative indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf is a particle of address.
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «ذلك».
﴿يدع﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿يدع﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿اليتيم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. The clause ﴿فذلك...﴾ is in the position of jussive as the answer of the implied condition.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿يحض﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿على طعام﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يحض﴾.
﴿المسكين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause ﴿لا يحض﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿يدع﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿فويل﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), i.e. "when you know that he is characterised by these qualities, then woe…" (إذا علمت أنه متصف بهذه الصفات فويل), or "when the matter is so, then woe…" (إذا كان الأمر كذلك فويل); or the fāʾ is resumptive; and «ويل» is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿للمصلين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المصلين» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿ويل للمصلين﴾ is the answer of the implied non-jussive condition, or resumptive, and on both views it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المصلين﴾.
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عن صلاتهم﴾: «عن» is a preposition, and «صلاة» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by «عن», the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and it is muḍāf, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ساهون﴾.
﴿ساهون﴾: khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause ﴿هم عن صلاتهم ساهون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين».

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of «المصلين».
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يراءون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿يراءون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «هم», and the clause ﴿هم يراءون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ويمنعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يمنعون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿الماعون﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يمنعون﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the first object of «يمنعون» is omitted, i.e. "they withhold small kindnesses from people" (يمنعون الناس الماعون), or "they withhold small kindnesses from those who ask" (يمنعون الطالبين الماعون); the clause ﴿يمنعون﴾ is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause ﴿يراءون﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
This is the clear reading. It is permissible for the hamza to come "between-between" (bayna bayna, i.e., softened), so you say أرأيت (with softened hamza), and أريت is permissible with the hamza dropped. From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: أَرَأَيْتَكَ, the kāf being an added mark of address. The between-between hamza is vowelled, of the same measure (as a full hamza), only lightened; thus said Sībawayh. As for the view of whoever said: it is neither quiescent nor vowelled, that is impossible, because if it is not quiescent it is vowelled, and if it is not vowelled it is quiescent; so on his view it would have to be both quiescent and vowelled. The evidence that it is vowelled is the poet's saying: [al-Basīṭ] 588-
أأن رأت رجلا أعشى أضرّ به ... ريب المنون ودهر مفند خبل
(Is it because she saw a dim-sighted man, harmed by the vicissitudes of fate and a time that weakens and deranges?)
If you said أأن (with full hamzas), the metre would be the same. The between-between hamza is often a subject of error, and it is among the most difficult things in grammar. Among the evidence for what we said is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ [al-Baqara: 6]: if the between-between hamza were quiescent, two quiescent letters would come together. Likewise in أرأيت, the yāʾ is quiescent and the between-between hamza is vowelled; and whoever makes it quiescent and gives the yāʾ kasra has brought something impermissible, with no justification and no construal in Arabic.
«أرأيت» may be from seeing with the eye, in which case there is no omission in the speech; or from seeing with the heart (knowing), in which case the implied form is: "Have you seen the one who denies the Judgement after the proofs have appeared to him — is he not deserving of the punishment of Allah?"

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Abū Rajāʾ read يَدَعُ الْيَتِيمَ without doubling, i.e., abandons him [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows the standard يَدُعُّ].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ (3): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., he does not take care over the feeding of the poor, nor command it.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: it is the one who prostrates and goes like this and like this, or turns to his right and his left.
Abū Jaʿfar said: More fitting than this view, because of the high standing of the one who held it and its soundness in Arabic, is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn [Translator's note: so in the text], from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Mālik: A man said to him: الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ (5) — is it the soul's talking (to itself) during prayer? He said: All of us experience that; rather it is the one who neglects it (by letting it pass) its time. And in a narration other than that of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Saʿd said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون, and he said: "Those who delay it beyond its time".

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: I.e., they do not pray out of fear of punishment nor in hope of reward, but so that the Muslims may see them and not shed their blood — and they are the hypocrites.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
The scholars have discussed its meaning, as was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from al-Farrāʾ: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: al-māʿūn is zakāt. This is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās with variation. And from Ibn ʿAbbās:
al-māʿūn is what people hand to one another (household utensils). Al-Farrāʾ reported from some of the Arabs that al-māʿūn is water, and recited:
[al-Wāfir] 589- يمجّ صبيره الماعون صبّا ("its white cloud spews out water in a downpour"); ṣabīruhu means its clouds. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views go back to one origin, and it is only the withholding [Translator's note: the text reads «الظن», evidently for «الضنّ», "stinginess"] of a small thing which one ought not to withhold; it is derived from al-maʿn, which is the small thing. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is for interrogation. (بالدين) is attached to (يكذّب). (the fāʾ) is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis of an implied condition. (الذي) is a relative in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك). (لا) is negative. (على طعام) is attached to (يحضّ)..
Clause: «رأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «يكذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «ذلك الذي ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you ask about him, then that is the one who ...
And the clause: «يدعّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
And the clause: «لا يحضّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يدعّ.

safi-cedvel:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(the fāʾ) is resumptive. (ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ. (للمصلين) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ويل. (الذين) is a relative in the position of genitive, a naʿt of المصلين – or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" –. (عن صلاتهم) is attached to (ساهون). The second (الذين) is like the first – or it follows the first as a badal –..
Clause: «ويل للمصلّين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «هم ... ساهون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «هم يراءون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
And the clause: «يراءون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
And the clause: «يمنعون ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يراءون.

* Morphology:
(7) الماعون: a name for the need, of things one benefits from in the house, whether trivial or valuable. It was said that its wazn is فاعول from المعن, which is the small thing – said by Quṭrub – or that it is on the wazn مفعول, by transposition; the original is a passive participle from عان يعون, and it should properly be معون, the original being معوون; then the ʿayn of the word was moved before its fāʾ, giving موعون; then the wāw was changed to alif because of the fatḥa before it: ماعون.

* Benefits:
- Urging on the māʿūn:
The scholars differed about the māʿūn. It is reported from ʿAlī that it is zakāt. Ibn Masʿūd said: the māʿūn is the axe, the bucket and the pot. Mujāhid said: the māʿūn is lending (ʿāriyya). ʿIkrima said: the māʿūn, at its highest, is the obligatory zakāt, and at its lowest, lending of goods. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī said: the māʿūn is all kindness that people exchange among themselves. The meaning of the verse: it is a prohibition of stinginess and a rebuke against it.
The scholars said: it is recommended for a man to keep in his house a good deal of what the neighbours need, so that he lends it to them and shows them kindness, and he may obtain the reward. [Translator's note: the source reads "ويجوز الثواب" (literally "and the reward is permitted"); translated as written, though "ويحوز" (obtains) may be intended.]

semin-durr:1-1.t:
Al-Kisāʾī read {أرَيْتَ} with the hamza dropped. Its verification was given earlier in Sūrat al-Anʿām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not the preferred reading, because dropping it is restricted to the imperfect, and «rayta» is not sound from the Arabs. What made it easier is the occurrence of the interrogative particle at the beginning of the sentence, and the like of it is:
4656 - صاحِ هل رَيْتَ أو سَمِعْتَ براعٍ ... رَدَّ في الضَّرْعِ ما قرى في العِلابِ
(O friend, have you seen or heard of a herdsman who put back into the udder what was gathered in the milk-bowls?)"
In this «أَرَأَيْتَ» there are two views. The first: that it is of sight (baṣariyya), so it takes one object, which is the relative noun, as if he had said: "have you seen the one who denies?" The second: that it has the meaning of "tell me", so it takes two objects; al-Ḥawfī implied it as "is he not deserving of punishment?", and al-Zamakhsharī as "who is he?". What shows this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «أَرَأَيْتَك» with the kāf of address, for the kāf does not attach to the verb of sight.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {فَذَلِكَ}: there are two views on it. The first: that the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, that is: "if you consider him, or if you seek knowledge of him, then that (is he)". The second: that it is a conjunction, «فذلك» being conjoined to «الذي يَكَذِّبُ», either as a conjoining of one entity to another entity or of one attribute to another attribute, and the answer of «أَرَأَيْتَ» is omitted because what follows indicates it, as if it had been said: "Tell me, and what do you say of the one who denies the recompense, and of the one who mistreats the orphan and does not feed the poor: is what he does good?" On the first view the demonstrative is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the relative noun after it is the khabar, or it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "he is that one", and the relative noun is its adjective (naʿt). On the second view it is accusative, being conjoined to what is accusative.
But the Shaykh rejected the second, saying: "So he made «ذلك» in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the object. This is an odd construction, like your saying 'I honoured the one who visits us, and that one who is kind to us'; what comes to mind first is that «فذلك» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. On the supposition of the accusative the implied form would be: 'I honoured the one who visits us, so I honoured that one who is kind to us.' The demonstrative in this supposition is not as firmly placed as what is eloquent, for there is no need to point to the one who visits us; rather, the eloquent form is: 'I honoured the one who visits us, and the one who is kind to us', or 'I honoured the one who visits us, so he is kind to us'. As for his saying 'either a conjoining of one entity to another entity', it is not sound, because «فذلك» is a pointing to «الذي يُكَذِّب», so they are not two entities, since what is pointed to by «ذلك» is one. As for his saying 'the answer of «أرأيتَ» is omitted', this is not called an answer; rather, it is in the position of the second object of «أرأيتَ». As for his implying 'is what he does good?', we do not know the interrogative hamza to enter «niʿma» or «biʾsa», for they are both declarations of praise or blame (inshāʾ), and the interrogative enters only on a report (khabar)." End of quotation.
The reply to his saying "the demonstrative is not firmly placed" and so on is that the difference between the two is that in the noble verse there is an interrogative, namely «أرأيتَ», so it is good that it should explain what is asked about, unlike the example he gave; hence the stated construction is good. And to his saying "because «فذلك» is a pointing to «الذي يُكَذِّب»", by refusal: rather it points to what comes after it, as you say "Strike Zayd, and that standing one", a pointing to the standing one and not to Zayd, though it may be a pointing to him. And to his saying "it is not called an answer": the grammarians say "the answer of the interrogative", and this has been preceded by an interrogative, so that is good. And to his saying "the interrogative enters only on a report": by counter-argument with His saying {فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ} [Muḥammad: 22], for «ʿasā» is an inshāʾ, and what is a valid answer for him is a valid answer for us.
The majority read with ḍamma on the dāl and shadda on the ʿayn, from «daʿʿahu», that is, he pushed him away. The Commander of the Believers, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «يَدَعُ» with fatḥa on the dāl and without shadda on the ʿayn, that is, he leaves and neglects. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ولا يُحاضُّ», from «muḥāḍḍa», which was treated in [Sūrat] al-Fajr.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ}: the khabar of His saying «فوَيْلٌ»; the fāʾ is for causation (li-l-tasabbub), that is: from these blameworthy attributes follows the invocation of woe upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after his saying "as if it had been said: 'tell me, and what do you say of the one who denies the religion', up to 'is what he does good?'": "Then Allah the Exalted said {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ}, that is, when it is known that he is an evildoer: woe to the worshippers, in the sense 'woe to them', except that He put their attribute in the place of their pronoun, because they were, together with the denial and what is annexed to it, heedless of the prayer, showing off, not paying zakāt on their wealth. If you ask: how did you make «المُصَلِّين» stand in the place of the pronoun of 'the one who denies', who is singular? I say: because its meaning is plural, since what is meant by it is the kind (al-jins)."
The Shaykh said: "As for his putting «المُصَلِّين» in the place of the pronoun, and «المُصَلِّين» being plural because the pronoun of 'the one who denies' is plural in meaning, it is an evident affectation. The Qurʾān should be taken only on what the apparent sense gives, and it is the habit of this man to affect things in understanding the Qurʾān that are not clear." End of quotation. I say: it is the habit of our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, to be biased against al-Zamakhsharī until he makes his good appear ugly. How can what he said be rejected, when it has the interlinking of the discourse, each part to the other, making it a single thing, and the intensification of the threat that it contains in bringing out their shameful description? There is no doubt that the apparent sense of the discourse is that the whole sūra describes a people who combined all of these attributes: denying the religion, repelling the orphan, not urging the feeding of the poor, heedlessness in prayer, showing off, and withholding what is good.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {الذين هُمْ}: it may be in the position of the nominative, or the accusative, or the genitive as a follower, either an adjective (naʿt), a badal or a bayān; likewise the second relative noun, except that it may be a follower of «المُصَلِّيْنَ» or a follower of the first relative noun. His saying «يُراؤُون»: its original is «yurāʾiyūna», like «yuqātilūna». The meaning of murāʾāt is that the one who shows off (al-murāʾī) shows people his deed, and they show him praise of it, so the reciprocity (mufāʿala) in it is clear. The verification of this was given earlier.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الماعون}: there are several views. The first: that it is of the form fāʿūl from «al-maʿn», which is the little thing. One says «māluhu maʿna», that is, little; Quṭrub said this. The second: that it is a passive participle of «aʿānahu, yuʿīnuhu»; the original is «maʿwūn». On this it ought by right to be said «maʿūn», like «maqūl» and «maṣūn», passive participles of «qāla» and «ṣāna», but the word was inverted, its ʿayn being put before its fāʾ, so that it became «mawʿūn»; then the first wāw was changed to alif, as they say «tāba» and «ṣāma» for «tawba» and «ṣawma», so its pattern is now «maʿfūl» [Translator's note: so printed in the source, evidently «mafʿūl» in its inverted form]. In this view there is irregularity in three respects. The first: that a form mafʿūl has come from af ʿala, whereas by right it should be on mufʿal, like mukram, so that one would say «muʿān», like «muqām»; mafʿūl is the passive participle of the triliteral. The second: the inversion, which is contrary to the original. The third: changing the weak letter to alif although it is not vowelled, and analogizing it on «tāba» and «ṣāma» is remote, because of the irregularity of what is analogized upon. The third may be answered by saying that the wāw was vowelled in the original before the inversion, since it is on the pattern of «maʿwūn».
The third of the first views: that its original is «maʿūna» and the alif is a replacement for the hāʾ; its pattern is «mafʿul», like «malūm», and its pattern after the addition is «mā fuʿl». The expressions of the commentators differed on it, and the best of them is that it is everything that is used for help and benefit, like the axe, the bucket and the fire-striker. The saying of al-Aʿshā was recited:
4657 - بأَجْوَدَ مِنْه بماعُوْنِه ... إذا ما سماؤُهمُ لم تَغِمّْ
(. . . more generous than he with his utensils, when their sky does not become overcast.)
He did not mention the first object of "withholding", either because it is known, that is, "they withhold from people or from those who ask", or because the aim is to mention what they withhold and not those from whom they withhold, as a reminder of their meanness and their stinginess with trivial things, the withholding of which is held ugly by everyone.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَذَلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (فَذَلِكَ): the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, its implied form being: «إِنْ تَأَمَّلْتَهُ» (if you consider him), or «إِنْ طَلَبْتَ عِلْمَهُ» (if you seek to know him). (يَدُعُّ), with a doubled consonant, means «يَدْفَعُ» (he repulses).
It has also been read with a fatḥa on the dāl and a single (undoubled) ʿayn, i.e. he neglects him. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Dīn
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أرَأيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ ("have you seen the one who denies the Judgement?"): it was also read ”أرَيْتَ“. The preferred [reading] is ”أرَأيْتَ“ with the second hamza retained, because the hamza is dropped only in the imperfect, in ”تَرى“, ”يَرى“ and ”أرى“, the original forms being ”تَرْأى“ and ”يَرْأى“. As for ”رَأيْتُ“, ”رَيْتُ“ is not soundly reported from the Arabs in it; but since the interrogative alif is at the beginning of the utterance, it made dropping the hamza easier. The preferred [course] is to retain it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿يَدُعُّ اليَتِيمَ﴾ ("repulses the orphan"): the meaning of ”يَدُعُّ“ in the language is "he pushes away"; and likewise His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 13] ("the Day they will be shoved into the Fire of Hell with a shove"), that is, they are pushed into it violently. So that is the one who pushes the orphan away from his right.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ﴾ ("and does not urge the feeding of the poor"): that is, he does not feed the poor nor command that he be fed. It is also read: ”فَذَلِكَ الَّذِي يَدَعُ اليَتِيمَ“ ("that is the one who leaves the orphan"), whose interpretation is: that is the one who pays no heed to the orphan and leaves him neglected.

zajjaj:5-6.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ هم عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ هم يُراءُونَ﴾ ("who are heedless of their prayer, who make a show"): by this the hypocrites are meant, because they made a show of prayer only: when the believers saw them, they prayed with them, and when they did not see them, they did not pray. And it was said: "they are heedless of their prayer" [means] they delay it beyond its time; and whoever deliberately delays it beyond its time until the time of another [prayer] comes in, woe to him also, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَمْنَعُونَ الماعُونَ﴾ ("and withhold small kindnesses"): that is, they withhold that in which there is benefit. ”اَلْماعُونُ“ in the Jāhiliyya was whatever has benefit in it, even the axe, the bucket, the cooking-pot and the fire-striker, and everything from which benefit is derived, little or much. Al-Aʿshā said:
بِأجْوَدَ مِنهُ بِماعُونِهِ ∗∗∗ إذا ما سَماؤُهم لَمْ تَغِمْ
(…[is not] more generous than he with his māʿūn when their sky gives no cloud [i.e. in drought].)
And ”اَلْماعُونُ“ in Islam: it was said that it is the zakāt and obedience. Al-Rāʿī said:
قَوْمِي عَلى الإسْلامِ لَمّا يَمْنَعُوا ∗∗∗ ماعُونَهم ويُضَيِّعُوا التَّهْلِيلا
(My people, upon Islam, have not withheld their māʿūn [zakāt] nor neglected the declaration of Allah's oneness.)
